I only have 1.5 mu, so I will manage it carefully and keep it simple. I grow only cotton, and I will mostly start from what worked before. With my small area, I can afford to watch the field closely, and since I have well irrigation, I do not need to gamble too much on rain. I have middle school education, so I do look at what seed dealers say and what nearby farmers plant, but I still trust what I have seen in the village. For seed, I will use improved cotton seed, not old saved seed, because the stand is usually more even and the bolls set better. For fertilizer, I will not go light, because if cotton grows weak early, it is hard to make up later. I will put enough base fertilizer first, then topdress again when the plants are growing strongly and starting to set squares. Since money is tight on a 1.5 mu plot, I will not chase fancy products, but I will make sure nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium are all there. I will plough before planting because cotton roots do better in loose soil, and I will irrigate around four times if the season is normal: once after sowing if moisture is short, once at seedling to early growth, once at flowering, and once at boll setting. For pests, I will plan on about five sprays in the year, because cotton in our area often needs control for aphids, bollworm, and mites. If the season goes smoothly, I will aim for about 320 kg per mu of seed cotton.
